summary.headline: Rolex Rings FY26 revenue held flat at INR1,144 crore despite a ~30% U.S. export drop; FY27 guided to 15-17% growth.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was about INR1,144 crore, broadly flat year on year, as a roughly 30% fall in U.S. exports was offset by Europe growth of about 25% and domestic growth of about 50%. Gross margin rose to 51.5% from 49.4%, attributed mainly to product mix, and operating EBITDA was held above 20%. Q4 other expenses were inflated by about INR22 crore of U.S. customs duty (about half recoverable from customers) and about INR6 crore of one-time legal and professional costs tied to the lender settlement. The company completed the INR101 crore Right of Recompense payment to lenders on March 31, 2026, and announced a INR180 crore buyback at INR180 per share, from which promoters are not participating.

segments.name: Domestic bearing rings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR386 crore vs INR329 crore in FY25, about 17-18% growth. Management puts the company's share of the domestic hot-forging bearing ring market at about 30%, within a INR1,600-1,800 crore addressable market.

segments.name: Domestic auto components
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR170 crore vs INR177 crore in FY25, a decline of about 4%.

segments.name: Export bearing rings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR154 crore vs INR155 crore in FY25, broadly flat.

segments.name: Export auto components
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR350 crore vs INR399 crore in FY25, a decline of about 12%, driven by the U.S. tariff disruption. Auto components are about 50% of revenue.

segments.name: Scrap and export incentives
segments.commentary: FY26 scrap revenue INR71 crore (FY25: INR78 crore) and export incentives INR13 crore (FY25: INR16 crore).

segments.name: Geography mix (FY26, % of revenue)
segments.commentary: U.S. about 23%, Europe about 22%, Mexico/Canada/others about 2%, and domestic about 54%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15-17%, with high-teens growth expected in FY28. This excludes recovery of U.S. volumes lost in FY26.
Management expects at least 50% of the ~30% lost U.S. business to return in H1 FY27, with the rest in H2.
About INR160-165 crore of revenue expected in FY27 from the pending INR175 crore order pipeline, excluding programmes on hold in the U.S.
Operating EBITDA guided to not fall below 20.5-21%, with upside from scale and fixed-cost absorption. Gross margin range guided at 49-53%.
Customs duty recovery (IEEPA-era, up to Oct 31, 2025) to be booked as revenue when received, expected by about September 2026. Not included in guidance.
Capex of about INR30-40 crore minimum plus maintenance, roughly INR50 crore a year for FY27 and FY28. Dividend under consideration after the buyback.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 62-63% overall, with some product lines at 80-85%, which need year-on-year capex.
Minimum capex of INR30-40 crore a year plus maintenance; split of about 70-75% forging and 25-30% machining and other capabilities.
Operates 26 forging lines and more than 625 CNC spindles under one setup.
Hot forging is the core route; cold forging is not planned near-term.
New programmes won in FY26 are ramping from 10-20% of peak volume toward 50-60% through FY27.
demand_pricing: Freight costs are rising. Container availability is delayed 2-3 weeks, managed through premium payments and warehouse/consignment stock. No order deferrals reported since March 2026.
Raw material pass-through to most overseas customers is quarterly, with a couple of customers on half-yearly terms.
U.S. Section 232 duty on the company's products is 25%, with some industrial bearings at 18%. The Supreme Court ruling does not cover Section 232. Customers have accepted the 25% rate.
Europe growth is mostly from passenger and light commercial vehicles (about 70%), with about 25-30% from industrial. Over 60% of new nominations came from European customers.
Domestic demand is mixed: four of six large domestic customers are growing, but industrial and large-size bearings are stagnant. Import substitution is under way.
EV exposure is limited. Overseas customers are focused on ICE and hybrid programmes, and management sees EV as a 5-7 year story.
Top five customer groups account for about 65-70% of business, spanning more than 15 plants. Wallet share is 45-50% with the top three bearing makers and 35-40% with certain auto-component customers.

qa_highlights.question: Are geopolitical issues and freight costs causing order delays?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferrals so far. Customers have returned to original schedules since March 2026. Container delays of 2-3 weeks are being managed with premiums and inventory buffers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 segment breakup and the FY25 comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26: domestic bearing rings INR386 crore, domestic auto components INR170 crore, export bearing rings INR154 crore, export auto components INR350 crore. FY25: INR329 crore, INR177 crore, INR155 crore, INR399 crore respectively.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth expectations and what drove Q4 gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guided at 15-17% and high-teens in FY28. Margin expansion attributed mainly to product mix and a shift from overseas to domestic steel on some processes. Customs duty recoveries booked in Q2-Q3 were also in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex and dividend policy look given the INR367 crore cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum capex of INR30-40 crore a year plus maintenance, about INR50 crore in total. Cash will be retained for now. Buyback of INR180 crore is first; dividends are under consideration afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customs duty treatment and refund outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR22 crore of duty was expensed in Q4, roughly half recoverable from customers. Duty paid under IEEPA until October 31, 2025 may be refunded, while 25% Section 232 duty is not refundable. Refund amounts to be booked as revenue when received.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and inventory position?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly dispatches of INR115-125 crore are planned for H1 FY27. Ex-transit inventory is 70-85 days, or 150-160 days including goods in transit under Incoterms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for sustainable margins and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected in the 49-53% range. Operating EBITDA should not go below 20.5-21%. Domestic market share of about 30% could rise to 50% in 1.5-2 years, with domestic bearing ring revenue growing 10-15% a year.

risks_watch: U.S. recovery depends on customers rebuilding inventory. Several programmes from the INR175 crore pipeline remain on hold and are excluded from FY27 estimates.
Freight and container availability disruptions from geopolitical events, plus rising European conversion, power and labour costs.
Q1-Q2 FY27 receipt of U.S. customs duty recoveries, and the status of refund claims under IEEPA litigation.
Domestic industrial and large-bearing demand is stagnant. Domestic auto components fell about 4% in FY26.
Inventory days, which would be 150-160 including in-transit sales, against 70-85 excluding in-transit goods.
Early-stage exploration of inorganic opportunities using surplus cash. Dividend policy is not yet set.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and growth, with conservative numerical guidance and explicit caution on U.S. timing and geopolitics. Management was less precise on the refund amount and on the timing of U.S. volume recovery, which it tied to customer inventory rebuilds.
key_quotes: The 30% revenue decline we experienced in the U.S. through FY 2026 is entirely recoverable and the pace of recovery will depend on how quickly our customers rebuild their inventory pipelines and production schedules.
We have not lost a single U.S. customer. These are long-standing relationships with leading global customer base and the programs are intact.
I expect on a conservative way, operating EBITDA would not be less than 20.5%, 21% kind of thing.

adds.what: Minimum INR30-40 crore a year capex (approx. 70-75% forging, 25-30% machining) with no specific new plant, line or capacity addition named

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-17% (midpoint 16%), backed partly by a INR175 crore pending order pipeline (INR160-165 crore expected in FY27), ramping new programmes and expected U.S. volume recovery (at least 50% of ~30% lost U.S. business in H1 FY27), but no specific new capacity is named and utilisation is only 62-63%.
